summary: OpenAI's status page reported increased server-overload errors affecting Codex 5.6-sol on 17 July 2026. The page listed the issue as identified at 17:19, said mitigation had been applied and recovery was being monitored at 19:07, and reported all impacted services fully recovered at 20:42; the retrieved page does not state the timezone for those displayed times. User reports corroborated capacity and server_overloaded symptoms, while later recurrence was kept separate from the original incident window.

assessment_boundaries: The status page does not publish a detailed technical postmortem.
Later user-reported recurrence is not treated as additional duration for the original incident.
No current taxonomy class is forced onto a capacity symptom without its recognition conditions.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's status record identifies increased server-overload errors affecting Codex 5.6-sol. The page displays updates at 17:19 (identified), 19:07 (mitigation applied and monitoring), and 20:42 (all impacted services fully recovered) on 17 July 2026; the retrieved page does not state the timezone for those displayed times. User testimony corroborates 'Selected model is at capacity' and server_overloaded symptoms but is not used to extend the original outage window or infer an internal capacity mechanism beyond the provider's stated overload condition.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a model-capacity degradation with a known surface condition, not evidence that account, entitlement, policy or verification states were collapsed. Governance still benefits from exposing capacity as the operative state so users do not misdiagnose the failure as loss of authority or access rights.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000017 demonstrates that not every service failure belongs in a failure taxonomy. Precise operational state can itself be the correct governance response when public evidence does not establish a reusable internal failure mechanism.
